newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee flat, dealers watch Central Bank.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee flat, dealers watch Central Bank.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed unmoved in ranged trade, as dealers were wary of the Central Bank's reaction to an overseas dollar correction, and a lack of import demand or incentives to build positions, dealers said.
The rupee closed at its opening level of 57.55, after moving between 57.54-57.60. The rupee closed at 57.52 on Friday.
"There was no import demand to boost the dollar. It was not possible to use low call rates to build pluses, since the rate was near the Central Bank top," said a Deutsche Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 4.75 local cents, fixing buying and selling at 56.5290 and 57.6710, despite the U.S. currency being unchanged overseas, dealers said.

A Citibank dealer said the current exchange rate was more suitable for selling dollars, than for buying them. "But since the Central Bank has been putting up the dollar aggressively, no one wants to sell the currency either."
Overnight call, meanwhile remained low and closed at 12.25 percent after opening at 13, dealers said.

The market is well offered, and dealers expect rates to stay low after the Central Bank relaxed monetary policy and cut statutory reserves by one percent, and allowed exporters to borrow in foreign currency, earlier this month.
Forward dollar premiums too have taken a dip mirroring a decline in interest rates, said the Citibank dealer.
